title: SEST on La Silla
caption: The Swedish-ESO Submillimeter Telescope backlit by the Moon, La Silla Observatory
celestial: Landscape photograph; the source does not name the site

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: The 15-meter dish of the Swedish-ESO Submillimeter Telescope, known as SEST, fills the center of this photograph, lit from behind by the Moon. Farther away on the right, at the highest point of the mountain, stands the dome of the ESO 3.6-meter telescope.

The antenna dish is so highly polished that it acts like a curved mirror. It holds an upside-down reflection of the sky and of the horizon behind the photographer, so the picture shows two views at once.

The source also names two sky features. The reddish star at the top right is Aldebaran, in the constellation Taurus. The Pleiades star cluster appears just to the right of SEST, at about the two o'clock position. As its name says, SEST was built to observe submillimeter wavelengths, far longer than those the eye can see.

understand.summary: This is a moonlit landscape photograph credited to ESO. The source gives no camera or color details.
understand.eye: The telescope itself was built for wavelengths the eye cannot see, while this photograph records ordinary visible light.
